subject: Order form & tax — final pricing cadence and invoice path
content:
From: Charlotte Evans <charlotte@pulsewave.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@pulsewave.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@pulsewave.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: PulseWave order form + tax questions

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is the order form draft (pulsewave_orderform_proposal_20280320.pdf) and our finance team’s tax questionnaire. A few items we need clarified before legal will sign:

- Confirmation of invoice entity and bank wiring instructions (we sometimes need invoice to come from a different Redwood legal entity).
- Net terms: client prefers Net45 for large inaugural commitments — can Redwood accept Net45 with an upfront credit to cover the first 30 days?
- VAT/reverse-charge: PulseWave is EU-registered and will apply reverse-charge where allowed; we’ll need Redwood to accept reverse-charge treatment and provide a VAT invoice.
- Activation fee: we expected a single activation fee to be invoiced at commencement and not pro-rated; confirm that.
- PO requirements: our procurement team requires the PO number printed on the invoice and a single consolidated invoice per quarter where possible.

Attaching: pulsewave_orderform_proposal_20280320.pdf and our procurement checklist. Please loop in sales/legal as needed.

Best,
Charlotte Evans
Head of Procurement, PulseWave Systems

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Charlotte Evans <charlotte@pulsewave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PulseWave order form + tax questions

Charlotte — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and next steps: 

- Invoice entity: we can invoice from Redwood Inference, Inc. (US entity) or Redwood Inference EU SARL (EU entity). Please confirm which legal entity you need on the invoice and the remit-to bank details. If you require EU entity invoices, we’ll route billing through our EU ops (may affect tax treatment).

- Net terms: we can do Net45 for the first agreement if we align on an upfront credit that covers month 1; finance will require a schedule of expected consumption so we can size the credit. Ben — can you propose the credit/commit structure?

- VAT/reverse-charge: happy to accept reverse-charge where applicable, but we’ll need your VAT number and a signed VAT self-assessment form. Karthik/legal — please advise on any wording we should add to the order form to support reverse-charge.

- Activation fee: we can invoice activation fee at commencement and mark it non-prorated — will confirm final language in the order form appendix.

- PO on invoice & consolidated invoices: we can include PO numbers and offer quarterly consolidated invoices; if PulseWave prefers per-entity consolidation we’ll need a mapping of which business units map to which PO.

Attachments: I added a tracked-redline of the order form focusing on pricing cadence and invoice routing (redline_orderform_kp_20280320.docx).

Next steps: Ben to propose a phased minimum-commit cadence and upfront credit number; Karthik & Laura to propose a short tax/withholding clause to add to the order form. I’ll coordinate the DocuSign milestone once legal signs off.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

---

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Charlotte Evans <charlotte@pulsewave.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PulseWave order form + tax questions

Appreciate the clear checklist, Charlotte. A proposed commercial approach below (high level):

Summary proposal:
- Pricing banding: Tiered unit pricing by monthly usage bands; $0.018/token for 0-1M, $0.014/token for 1-5M, $0.011/token 5M+ (draft, subject to consumption profile).
- Minimum commit phasing: Year 1 commit of $750K split into three tranches (Q1: $250K, Q3: $250K, Q4: $250K) to give you runway and align to launch milestones.
- Upfront credit: Redwood will provide a $100K upfront credit to be applied to invoices over the first 60 days (covers first-month volatility).
- Net terms: We can accept Net45 on invoices provided the upfront credit is executed and outstanding balance below credit threshold is paid per Net45 thereafter.
- Activation fee: one-time $25K invoiced at commencement (non-prorated).
- Consolidated invoices: we can issue consolidated quarterly invoices and include the PO number on each line item.

I’ve attached the revised order form with the proposed pricing table (orderform-v3.pdf). If the above looks directionally correct, I’ll bake the numbers into the HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign envelope for signature once legal confirms language.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876 (DEAL PW-2028-9876)
DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/xyz-pulsewave-orderform

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachment: orderform-v3.pdf (pricing table, commit phasing)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Charlotte Evans <charlotte@pulsewave.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PulseWave order form + tax questions

Thanks all — I reviewed the attached orderform-v3.pdf and Kimberly’s redline. A few legal redlines/notes to close procurement’s checklist quickly: 

1) Tax & withholding clause: add a short paragraph to the order form: 
   "Taxes and Withholding: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, customer shall be responsible for value-added taxes, sales taxes or similar taxes imposed by applicable law. Where Customer asserts reverse charge, Customer must provide valid tax registration evidence and a completed tax self-declaration form prior to first invoice. If Redwood is required by law to withhold taxes, Customer shall provide documentation to avoid gross-up; absent timely evidence, Redwood reserves the right to gross-up invoiced amounts to account for withholding obligations."

2) Invoice entity: please confirm whether PulseWave requires Redwood Inference EU SARL on the invoice. If yes, we will trigger our EU billing flow which typically takes 5 business days to set up.

3) Net terms and credit: legal okay with Net45 provided the upfront credit is contractually reflected as a prepayment credit line with defined application timeline. We should include a short schedule (appendix A) that spells out credit drawdown mechanics.

4) SLA credits & rollback: if you require SLA-specific credits in the MSA we need to scope whether credits offset invoices (preferred) or produce separate credit memos; keep that in mind for finance reconciliation.

I’ve attached a redlined MSA excerpt with the tax/withholding language (msa-redline-karthik_20280322.docx). Laura — can you do a one-pass on the sample clause and confirm?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel (Commercial), Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Charlotte / Procurement — thanks, all of this is actionable. Quick summary and next steps: 

- Ben will update HubSpot and send the DocuSign envelope with the priced order form (Ben: target EOD Fri).
- PulseWave to confirm invoice entity (US vs EU) and provide VAT number + signed tax self-declaration form (we can send a template).
- Karthik/Laura to finalize the tax/withholding clause and appendix A (credit drawdown mechanics).
- Kimberly to confirm activation fee invoice timing and whether PulseWave wants quarterly consolidated invoices (default is yes).

If you can confirm entity and VAT number today, we’ll try to route EU invoices and have finance standing by to set the Net45 credit. Otherwise, we’ll proceed with US entity invoices and the same commercial terms but note VAT will be handled differently.

Thanks — appreciate the speedy turnaround.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
